In [[mathematics]], '''Schilder's theorem''' is a generalization of the [[Laplace's method|Laplace method]] from integrals on <math>\mathbb{R}^n</math> to functional Wiener integration. The theorem is used in the [[large deviations theory]] of [[stochastic process]]es.  Roughly speaking, out of Schilder's theorem one gets an estimate for the probability that a (scaled-down) sample path of [[Brownian motion]] will stray far from the mean path (which is constant with value 0).  This statement is made precise using [[rate function]]s.  Schilder's theorem is generalized by the [[Freidlin–Wentzell theorem]] for [[Itō diffusion]]s.
==Statement of the theorem==
Let ''C''<sub>0</sub>&nbsp;=&nbsp;''C''<sub>0</sub>([0,&nbsp;''T''];&nbsp;'''R'''<sup>''d''</sup>) be the Banach space of continuous functions  <math> f : [0,T] \longrightarrow \mathbf{R}^d</math> such that <math>f(0)=0</math>, equipped with the [[supremum norm]] ||&sdot;||<sub>&infin;</sub> and <math>C_0^\ast</math> be the subspace of absolutely continuous functions whose derivative is in <math>L^2</math> (the so-called [[Cameron–Martin theorem|Cameron-Martin space]]). Define the rate function 
:<math>I(\omega) = \frac{1}{2} \int_{0}^{T} \| \dot{\omega}(t) \|^{2} \, \mathrm{d} t</math>
on <math>C_0^\ast</math> and let <math>F:C_0\to\mathbb{R},G:C_0\to\mathbb{C}</math> be two given functions, such that <math>S:=I+F</math> (the "action") has a unique minimum <math>\Omega\in C_0^\ast</math>.

Then under some differentiability and growth assumptions on <math>F,G</math> which are detailed in [https://doi.org/10.2307/1994588 Schilder 1966], one has 
:<math>\lim_{\lambda\to\infty}\frac{\mathbb{E}\left[\exp\left(-\lambda F(\lambda^{-1/2} \omega)\right)G(\lambda^{-1/2} \omega)\right]}{\exp\left(-\lambda S(\Omega)\right)} = G(\Omega)\mathbb{E}\left[\exp\left(-\frac{1}{2}\langle\omega, D(\Omega) \omega\rangle\right)\right]</math> 

where <math>\mathbb{E}</math> denotes expectation with respect to the Wiener measure <math>\mathbb{P}</math> on <math>C_0</math> and <math>D(\Omega)</math> is the Hessian of <math>F</math> at the minimum <math>\Omega</math>; <math>\langle\omega, D(\Omega) \omega\rangle</math> is meant in the sense of an <math>L^2([0,T])</math> inner product.

==Application to large deviations on the Wiener measure==
Let ''B'' be a standard Brownian motion in ''d''-[[dimension]]al [[Euclidean space]] '''R'''<sup>''d''</sup> starting at the origin, 0&nbsp;&isin;&nbsp;'''R'''<sup>''d''</sup>; let '''W''' denote the [[law (stochastic processes)|law]] of ''B'', i.e. classical [[Wiener measure]].  For ''&epsilon;''&nbsp;&gt;&nbsp;0, let '''W'''<sub>''&epsilon;''</sub> denote the law of the rescaled process {{radic|''&epsilon;''}}''B''.  Then, on the [[Banach space]] ''C''<sub>0</sub>&nbsp;=&nbsp;''C''<sub>0</sub>([0,&nbsp;''T''];&nbsp;'''R'''<sup>''d''</sup>) of continuous functions  <math> f : [0,T] \longrightarrow \mathbf{R}^d</math> such that <math>f(0)=0</math>, equipped with the [[supremum norm]] ||&sdot;||<sub>&infin;</sub>, the [[probability measure]]s '''W'''<sub>''&epsilon;''</sub> satisfy the large deviations principle with good rate function ''I''&nbsp;:&nbsp;''C''<sub>0</sub>&nbsp;&rarr;&nbsp;'''R'''&nbsp;&cup;&nbsp;{+&infin;} given by

:<math>I(\omega) = \frac{1}{2} \int_{0}^{T} | \dot{\omega}(t) |^{2} \, \mathrm{d} t</math>

if ''&omega;'' is [[absolutely continuous]], and ''I''(''&omega;'')&nbsp;=&nbsp;+&infin; otherwise.  In other words, for every [[open set]] ''G''&nbsp;&sube;&nbsp;''C''<sub>0</sub> and every [[closed set]] ''F''&nbsp;&sube;&nbsp;''C''<sub>0</sub>,

:<math>\limsup_{\varepsilon \downarrow 0} \varepsilon \log \mathbf{W}_{\varepsilon} (F) \leq - \inf_{\omega \in F} I(\omega)</math>

and

:<math>\liminf_{\varepsilon \downarrow 0} \varepsilon \log \mathbf{W}_{\varepsilon} (G) \geq - \inf_{\omega \in G} I(\omega).</math>

==Example==
Taking ''&epsilon;''&nbsp;=&nbsp;1/''c''<sup>2</sup>, one can use Schilder's theorem to obtain estimates for the probability that a standard Brownian motion ''B'' strays further than ''c'' from its starting point over the time interval [0,&nbsp;''T''], i.e. the probability

:<math>\mathbf{W} (C_0 \smallsetminus \mathbf{B}_c (0; \| \cdot \|_\infty)) \equiv \mathbf{P} \big[ \| B \|_\infty > c \big],</math>

as ''c'' tends to infinity.  Here '''B'''<sub>''c''</sub>(0;&nbsp;||&sdot;||<sub>&infin;</sub>) denotes the [[open ball]] of radius ''c'' about the zero function in ''C''<sub>0</sub>, taken with respect to the [[supremum norm]].  First note that

:<math>\| B \|_\infty > c \iff \sqrt{\varepsilon} B \in A := \left \{ \omega \in C_0 \mid |\omega(t)| > 1 \text{ for some } t \in [0, T] \right\}.</math>

Since the rate function is continuous on ''A'', Schilder's theorem yields

:<math>\begin{align}
\lim_{c \to \infty} \frac{\log \left (\mathbf{P} \left [ \| B \|_\infty > c \right] \right )}{c^2}  &= \lim_{\varepsilon \to 0} \varepsilon \log \left (\mathbf{P} \left[ \sqrt{\varepsilon} B \in A \right] \right ) \\[6pt]
&= - \inf \left\{ \left. \frac{1}{2} \int_0^T | \dot{\omega}(t) |^2 \, \mathrm{d} t \,\right|\, \omega \in A \right\} \\[6pt]
&= - \frac{1}{2} \int_0^T \frac{1}{T^2} \, \mathrm{d} t \\[6pt]
&= - \frac{1}{2 T},
\end{align}</math>

making use of the fact that the [[infimum]] over paths in the collection ''A'' is attained for {{math|''&omega;''(''t'') {{=}} {{sfrac|''t''|''T''}}}} .  This result can be heuristically interpreted as saying that, for large {{math|''c''}} and/or large {{math|''T''}}

:<math>\frac{\log \left (\mathbf{P} \left [ \| B \|_\infty > c \right] \right )}{c^2} \approx - \frac{1}{2T} \qquad \text{or} \qquad \mathbf{P} \left[ \| B \|_\infty > c \right ] \approx \exp \left( - \frac{c^2}{2 T} \right).</math>

In fact, the above probability can be estimated more precisely:  for {{math|''B''}} a standard Brownian motion in {{math|'''R'''<sup>''n''</sup>}}, and any {{math|''T'', ''c''}} and {{math|''&epsilon;'' &gt; 0}}, we have:

:<math>\mathbf{P} \left[ \sup_{0 \leq t \leq T} \left| \sqrt{\varepsilon} B_t \right | \geq c \right] \leq 4 n \exp \left( - \frac{c^2}{2 n T \varepsilon} \right).</math>
